title: Ultralight Beam [V1]
description: Initial freestyle that would later be cut into the "night 1" arrangement by Fonzworth Bentley. Has the rough, unarranged Chance and Kanye vocals, with Justin Bieber's vocals coming in after the beat cuts out. He did not get to record a version separately, as he was handed the mic when the freestyle was happening. The song started as MIKE DEAN playing chords and DJDS in the corner of the room, presumably playing the sample that would later be covered by the choir. Then Swizz Beatz started programming drums, after which Fonzworth Bentley and Plain Pat went to a studio two blocks down and brought tambourines, which they started playing over the song every eight bars. After the instrumental had come together, the freestyle began, with Justin Bieber recording an acapella freestyle after the Chance and Kanye parts which were later cutdown.

title: YEEZY SLIDE KIDS
description: The adidas Yeezy Slide Kids ‘Desert Sand’ combines plush comfort with a futuristic, minimalist design, executed on a lightweight EVA build and finished in a refined hue. The unibody upper is stripped of any exterior branding, save for adidas’ three-stripe logo debossed on the cushioned footbed. An aggressive traction pattern distinguishes the outsole, delivering optimal grip and impact absorption underfoot.

title: YEEZY BOOST 350 V2
description: First released on April 29, 2017, the Yeezy Boost 350 V2 ‘Cream White’ combines a cream Primeknit upper with tonal cream SPLY 350 branding, and a translucent white midsole housing full-length Boost. Released again in October 2018, this retro helped fulfill Kanye West’s oft-repeated ‘YEEZYs for everyone’ Twitter mantra, as adidas organized the biggest drop in Yeezy history by promising pre-sale to anyone who signed up on the website. Similar to the first release, the ‘Triple White’ 2018 model features a Primeknit upper, a Boost midsole and custom adidas and Yeezy co-branding on the insole.
